about: Every visual asset QuestLayer can take as a drop-in file. Source for docs/ART-LIST.md (npm run art:list) and the file check (npm run art:check).

style.name: QuestLayer house style
style.prompt: QuestLayer game art: cute, friendly 2D fantasy-adventure illustration for a mobile map game. Chunky, instantly readable silhouette, thick dark plum outline (#1A0335), soft cel shading with two tones per colour, light from the upper left, a thin warm rim light. Palette: lavender #B9A6FF, hot pink #FA34F3, teal #37F4F1, mint #51FFA8, gold #FFD01F, deep purple #230E4F, cream #FFFAF0. Characters are QuestLayer's own round ghost folk with big glossy eyes and small pink cheeks. Single subject, centred, fully visible with a little empty margin, isolated on a transparent background, no text, no frame, no ground shadow.
style.negative: photorealistic, realistic 3D render, noise, text, letters, logo text, watermark, signature, busy background, scenery, floor, cast shadow on background, cropped limbs, cut-off edges, tiny details that disappear at 48 px, thin outlines, characters or logos from existing games or brands

groups.title: Auras (wearables)
groups.how: Only the effect, without the ghost. The game places 'above' Auras over the head and 'below' Auras on the ground. If a player wears an edition in the other slot, add <id>-above or <id>-below; otherwise the same file is fitted into the box. The game adds a gentle bob; no frames needed. NFT media on NEAR (public/aura-*.svg) stay unchanged on purpose: minted media must not change.
